title: Which Valuation Stands as the Marketplace Figure on a Class Move
content:
The value class a listing is moved into is not settled before a valuation dated within thirty calendar days of the handling date stands on the vehicle's condition record.

Which figure the marketplace then works from is read off the valuations standing on that Keyturn Vehicle Listing's condition record.

1. Where a valuation stands on the vehicle's condition record dated within 30 calendar days of the handling date, that valuation's amount is the marketplace figure.

2. Where none stands within 30 calendar days but at least one valuation stands on the record within the rolling twelve months counted back from the handling date, the highest valuation amount standing on the record is the marketplace figure.

3. Otherwise the vehicle value standing on the listing is the marketplace figure.

### Points of judgement

*Highest, not latest, on the second clause.* Where the second clause governs, the figure taken is the highest valuation amount standing on the condition record, and that is read across the record as a whole rather than across the twelve months alone; the twelve month window decides only whether the second clause is reached at all.

*At the day boundary.* A valuation dated exactly 30 calendar days before the handling date is within 30 calendar days and puts the vehicle on the first clause; one dated 31 calendar days before it does not.

*Where the record is empty.* A vehicle with no valuation standing on its condition record at all reaches the third clause, and the marketplace figure is the vehicle value standing on the listing itself.
